Folks — I ran the dry-run and one burst pass this morning against the mirror environment in us-west-2. Attaching a CSV with the sample run (20260221-orion-burst-results.csv). Highlights: 

- Steady-state (200 req/s, 30m): achieved 212 avg req/s; p50 = 72 ms; p95 = 310 ms; p99 = 540 ms. No 5xxs. TTFT measured at 48 ms median.
- Burst (1,000 req/s, 30s): sustained ~930 req/s for ~26s before queueing increased; observed queue depth spikes up to 14 requests and p95 jumped to 1.3s, p99 to 2.8s during peak. About 0.6% of requests experienced 429s due to server-side rate limiter bumping in aggressively at peak.
- Streams: with 30 concurrent streams active, TTFT increased ~20% under burst conditions versus baseline. Streaming tokens themselves were not the bottleneck; the main issue was CPU contention on the front-end nodes and tokenization concurrency.

Initial hypothesis: default rate limiter configuration is aggressively protecting downstream GPU queues, which prevents overload but causes short-lived client-visible 429s and elevated p99s. We see that increasing per-worker concurrency (and adding a small request queue allowance) smooths the peaks but increases median latency slightly.

Proposed infra tuning for next run: 
- Increase max_workers from 8 -> 12 for the test pool.
- Raise per-worker in-flight request cap from 4 -> 6.
- Add a short FIFO queue with max depth 50 and prioritize streaming TTFT-sensitive requests.

I'll schedule the next full battery for Feb 22 after we confirm these changes.

Thanks,
